newsitem.title: INDIA: India trade policy as scheduled - spokeswoman.
newsitem.headline: India trade policy as scheduled - spokeswoman.

text.p: India will announce its new export-import policy as scheduled on Monday, and the announcement will not be affected by political changes linked to the Congress party's withdrawal of support to the ruling coalition, a Commerce Ministry spokeswoman said on Sunday.
"The export-import policy cannot be postponed. The current policy expires tomorrow (Monday). A new exim policy has to take effect on April 1," the spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
"We are going ahead," the spokeswoman said.
Analysts expect India's new five-year trade policy to sweep away a battery of controls on imports and contain measures to revive flagging exports.

The export-import policy for 1997-2002 (April-March) is expected to be underpinned by India's pledge to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to liberalise imports and New Delhi's aim of aligning import tariffs with those of other fast-growing Asian nations.
India has agreed to present the WTO in June with a time-table to phase out restrictions on imports, and analysts say the trade policy would form the blueprint of the schedule.
Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on March 7 that he planned to present a "big, dynamic policy", in line with a market-oriented economic reforms programme launched in 1991.
On March 17, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram backed his claim, saying that easing curbs on consumer goods imports was an option that the government would decide on in the trade policy.
